title: still present since round 3: mark_opened applies the Submitted->UnderReview transition to ANY status, no guard
evidence: demo_store.gleam:1278-1290 'pub fn mark_opened( store: DemoStore, vacancy_id: String, application_id: String, ) -> #(DemoStore, Result(String, Nil)) { change_status( store, vacancy_id, application_id, "under_review", "status_auto_changed", ) }' — unconditional; no check of the current status anywhere in mark_opened or change_status. No test exercises mark_opened at all (grep 'mark_opened' over client/test/ = none).
detail: A mark_opened against an already-approved/rejected application silently moves it to under_review and appends a status_auto_changed audit entry; idempotency rests entirely on the dispatch-layer open_dispatched set, and the demo store path is untested.
recommended_fix: Transition only when current status is Submitted (otherwise return the unchanged store), and add a store-level boundary test: mark_opened on an Approved app is a no-op.

title: still present since round 3: vacancy/status mutations return Ok unconditionally — nonexistent ids report success, the Result error channel is dead
evidence: demo_store.gleam:1245 '(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(vacancy_id))' (archive_vacancy), :1259 (restore_vacancy), :1273 (close_vacancy) — all return Ok(vacancy_id) after a list.map that no-ops on miss. :1345 '#(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(slug))' (change_status — same shape). No test dispatches any mutation against a missing id (demo tests use seeded ids only).
detail: The map no-ops when nothing matches yet Ok is returned, so callers (and the toast layers they drive) cannot distinguish a miss from a mutation; the deliver_err path in demo_api is unreachable for these mutations.
recommended_fix: After the map, check find_vacancy/find_application on the result store and return Error(Nil) on miss (or drop the Result); add one missing-id test per mutation kind.

title: still present since round 3: status_from_slug silently coerces any unknown status slug to Submitted
evidence: demo_store.gleam:182-191 'fn status_from_slug(slug: String) -> ApplicationStatus { case slug { "submitted" -> Submitted "under_review" -> UnderReview "shortlisted" -> Shortlisted "viewed" -> Viewed "approved" -> Approved "rejected" -> Rejected _ -> Submitted } }' — the '_' fallback lands as Submitted.
detail: A typo in a demo action wire (e.g. 'shortlist') silently lands the application as Submitted rather than failing loudly; no test covers the fallback.
recommended_fix: Return Result or panic on unknown slugs (demo-only code), and pin one unknown-slug test.

title: still present since round 3: demo_not_in_demo_toast diverges from add_toast's id convention — the next add_toast reuses the demo toast's id
evidence: demo_update.gleam:638,645 'let toast_id = model.next_toast_id + 1 ... next_toast_id: toast_id,' while client.gleam add_toast:7115,7128 'let id = model.next_toast_id ... #(Model(..model, toasts: capped_toasts, next_toast_id: id + 1), dismiss_eff)'. After a demo toast at next_toast_id=N: toast id = N+1 and next_toast_id = N+1, so the following add_toast also uses id = N+1.
detail: Ids collide: the two toasts share one id, so one 5s AppDismissToast timeout dismisses both (the dismiss matches by id).
recommended_fix: Allocate demo toast ids via the same convention as add_toast (id = next_toast_id, then increment), or route through add_toast.
